title: FOIA REQUEST: Unmasking the DDOT "Ghost Inspector" (Falsified 311 Safety Records via Anonymous API)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TO: ddot.foia@dc.gov; ryann.sargent@dc.gov

CC: frank.seales@dc.gov; sharon.kershbaum@dc.gov; earl.eutsler@dc.gov; callen@dccouncil.gov; pmendelson@dccouncil.us
SUBJECT: FOIA REQUEST: Cityworks Backend Audit Log & Employee Unmasking (System ID 2600205)

To DDOT FOIA Officer Ryann Sargent:

Pursuant to the D.C. Freedom of Information Act, I request the immediate production of internal DDOT system records necessary to identify the District employee who falsified a public safety inspection.

On October 22, 2026, the Office of Unified Communications (OUC) released the backend Salesforce logs for 311 Service Request #26-00495403 regarding an active landslide and "Imminent Danger" tree hazard at 1490 Morris Rd SE.

The OUC logs confirm that this emergency safety ticket was closed in exactly 30 minutes with zero geolocated metadata, zero photographs from an arborist, and no evidence of a physical site visit. The ticket was closed using an anonymous API bridge account labeled "citizen Site Guest User."

However, the OUC logs prove that the ticket was routed to DDOT's internal management software. Specifically, the logs identify the External System Name as "CityWork-Open311Interface," the External Service Request as "ESR-0002726802," and the specific internal System Id as "2600205."

I demand the production of the native DDOT Cityworks backend audit log for System Id 2600205 / ESR-0002726802.

Specifically, this request demands:
1. The exact Active Directory login ID, employee name, and badge number of the DDOT employee who operated within Cityworks to mark this ticket as "Closed" on August 19, 2026.
2. The specific DDOT Urban Forestry Division employee or supervisor (including Branch Chief Duff McCully, if applicable) who authorized the use of the Cityworks API to administratively desk-reject an "Imminent Danger" landslide hazard using the false premise of a "private property" exemption, without conducting an active field inspection.

Fee Waiver Request: Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full fee waiver for this request. Disclosure of this information is in the immediate public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of municipal infrastructure failures, the falsification of environmental safety records, and agency non-compliance on Ward 8 Safe Schools Routes. I have no commercial interest in the disclosure of these records and am acting strictly in the capacity of a community advocate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR
